question: Should content-based routing become a built-in bindings config contract, or should core expose a generic pre-route route/body override for a plugin to implement it?
rationale: Current plugin hooks can inspect content but cannot reroute or rewrite the inbound agent body, while adding regex and stripping semantics directly to bindings creates public config, precedence, performance, and cross-channel commitments.

options.title: Add generic plugin seam
options.body: Extend the pre-route plugin contract with validated agent/session selection and agent-facing body replacement, then publish content routing as a plugin.

options.title: Add bounded core matcher
options.body: Add a deliberately limited prefix or safe-regex matcher to bindings with explicit precedence, cache bypass, normalization, and stripping contracts.

options.title: Keep dispatcher pattern
options.body: Decline new routing surface and continue using a default agent or custom middleware as the dispatcher.

recommendation.title: Add generic plugin seam
recommendation.body: Extend the pre-route plugin contract with validated agent/session selection and agent-facing body replacement, then publish content routing as a plugin.

likelyOwner.reason: The existing issue discussion and routing/config history make steipete the strongest available product-routing decision owner.
